title: #1 What is Project Management? Is it an Art or Science? | Project Planning & Control

best.what: defines a project as temporary + unique, contrasted with a repeating 'process', with relatable examples (exam vs. quiz, phone models)

why: the project-vs-process definition is a genuinely useful framing, but it's buried in a long call-and-response classroom discussion that spends its second half on 'is management art or science' (Taylor, Newton, Avogadro) which has nothing to teach a teen coder.

title: #7 Time Management | Overview | Project Planning & Control

best.what: work breakdown structure as 'divide and conquer': break a project into objectives, then activities, worked through a relatable example (organizing a guest lecture/event)

why: the WBS/divide-and-conquer idea and the worked event-planning example map directly onto breaking a solo app project into tasks and objectives; skip past the PMBOK/clause-number jargon in the first 3 minutes.

title: #38 Minimum Moment Concept | Project Planning & Control
why: pure resource-histogram-leveling math (moment formulas, improvement-factor derivation) for construction scheduling; explicitly the kind of engineering scheduling maths the brief excludes, no transfer to a teen planning an app.

title: #30 Time-Cost Trade-off: Problem- 3, Tabulation Approach | Project Planning & Control
why: CPM crashing worked problem with a cost-slope tabulation method; this is exactly the CPM-crashing/time-cost trade-off content the brief says does not transfer.

title: #5 Project Stakeholders, Phases & Organization | Project Planning & Control

best.what: stakeholders = everyone with a stake in a project, whose objectives you have to understand and balance
project life-cycle phases: idea -> business case -> pre-project planning -> execute -> operate -> decommission
cost-vs-influence curve: you can change things cheaply early, but changes get expensive once you're deep into building

why: the stakeholder concept, the phase list, and especially the 'decide early because changes get expensive later' curve transfer well to a teen's solo project (users = stakeholders, plan before you build); the rest is construction/EPC/refinery/subcontractor detail a teen doesn't need.
